title: Gradient integral bounded by Gaussian surface area
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $D(x)$ at every $x$, with $D$ continuous and $0\le f(x)\le1$ for all $x$. Suppose that for every real $\theta$, the Gaussian product integral of $|f(X)-f(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)|$ is at most the rotation sensitivity of $A$ at $\theta$, where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors. Then the Gaussian integral of $\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(x)e_i)^2}$ is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$.
hypotheses_covered: The rotation variation integral is at most the rotation sensitivity of $A$ for every real $\theta$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable and $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with continuous derivative $D(x)$. If $\mathbb E|f(G)-f(\cos\theta\,G+\sin\theta\,G\prime)|\le s_A(\theta)$ for every real $\theta$, then $\int\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\,d\gamma_n(x)\le P_\gamma(A)$ as a nonnegative extended integral.
